input.strategy_title: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

An accessibility audit found that four core Dashboard flows (project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) cannot be completed
with keyboard alone: focus is lost in modals, several controls are unreachable,
and focus indicators are inconsistent. Two public-sector customers require an
updated, published conformance statement (VPAT) before renewal — so the fixes
and the published documentation are both deliverables of this strategy.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require
- Flows outside the four audited ones

## Open Questions

None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow.

# Keyboard accessibility remediation for core Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic remediates the keyboard-accessibility defects identified by the
accessibility audit in the four core Dashboard flows — project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission — so that each
flow is fully operable by keyboard alone, with no focus traps, no unreachable
controls, and consistent visible focus indicators. It delivers the code fixes
in the Dashboard console that make the renewed conformance statement possible.

## Scope

- Remediate every keyboard-operability defect enumerated in the audit report
  for the four audited flows:
  - Eliminate focus loss and focus traps in modals and multi-step dialogs
    (focus must move into the modal on open, stay trapped while open, return
    to the invoking control on close).
  - Make every control in the four flows reachable and operable via keyboard
    (tab/shift-tab navigation, Enter/Space activation, arrow-key list
    traversal where the pattern requires it).
- Apply a consistent, visible focus-indicator style across all controls in the
  four audited flows, following the console UI kit's focus styling conventions
  rather than per-flow ad-hoc styles.
- Add automated keyboard-operability test coverage for the fixed defects in
  the four flows (keyboard walkthrough tests per flow), so regressions are
  caught by CI.
- Out of scope: screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes
  require, and flows outside the four audited ones.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the project creation flow, When a user completes it end-to-end using
  keyboard only, Then every step succeeds with no focus traps and no
  unreachable controls.
- Given the workbench spawn flow, When completed end-to-end using keyboard
  only, Then every step succeeds with no focus traps and no unreachable
  controls.
- Given the model deployment flow, When completed end-to-end using keyboard
  only, Then every step succeeds with no focus traps and no unreachable
  controls.
- Given the pipeline run submission flow, When completed end-to-end using
  keyboard only, Then every step succeeds with no focus traps and no
  unreachable controls.
- Given the audit report's defect list for the four flows, When each defect is
  re-checked via a keyboard-only walkthrough, Then every enumerated defect is
  resolved or explicitly dispositioned.
- Given any interactive control in the four audited flows, When it receives
  keyboard focus, Then a visible focus indicator is rendered using the shared
  focus styling convention, consistent across all four flows.
- Given the added keyboard-operability tests, When the full test suite and the
  console build pipeline run, Then they pass green.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)**: The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard,
  with no focus traps or unreachable controls — covered by the operability
  remediation and per-flow walkthrough ACs above.
- **HLR-2 (P1)**: Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited
  flows — covered by the shared focus-indicator styling scope and its AC.
  Bundled with HLR-1 by design: both requirements are satisfied by one
  remediation pass over the same audit defect list and the same UI surfaces.

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation

## Description

This epic updates and republishes the accessibility conformance documentation
— the VPAT conformance statement and the product documentation's accessibility
statement — to reflect the fixed keyboard-accessibility state of the four core
Dashboard flows, with technical review against the implemented behavior. This
is the deliverable two public-sector customers require before renewal.

## Scope

Content outline (authored in the Red Hat docs content process):

- **VPAT / conformance statement**: update the existing conformance statement
  so the claims for the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn,
  model deployment, pipeline run submission) reflect the remediated
  keyboard-operability and focus-indicator state, accurately representing any
  remaining exceptions (e.g. items out of scope: screen-reader semantics
  beyond keyboard fixes, flows outside the four audited ones).
- **Accessibility statement (product docs)**: update the product
  documentation's accessibility statement to match the renewed conformance
  claims, and republish both documents.
- **Technical review**: each updated document is technically reviewed by the
  Dashboard engineering team against the implemented fixes before
  publication.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the completed keyboard-accessibility fixes in the Dashboard, When the
  VPAT is updated, Then every conformance claim covering the four audited
  flows matches the implemented behavior, and remaining exceptions are stated
  accurately.
- Given the updated VPAT, When the product docs accessibility statement is
  revised, Then it is consistent with the VPAT claims and both are
  republished.
- Given the updated documents, When technical review is performed by the
  Dashboard engineering team against the implemented fixes, Then review
  findings are resolved and the review is recorded before publication.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P2)**: The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and
  product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect
  the fixed state, with technical review — this epic's entire scope.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9017

**Strategy:** Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows

**Triage outcome:** Not below-threshold — the scope spans two architecturally
distinct work streams (Dashboard code remediation in the odh-dashboard console,
plus substantive conformance-content authoring: VPAT rewrite and accessibility
statement republish), which warrant separate PR review cycles. Not docs-only —
the Dashboard component requires code changes. Full decomposition proceeds.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Keyboard accessibility remediation for core Dashboard flows | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Documentation | P2 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001[RHAISTRAT-9017-E001: Keyboard accessibility remediation]
    E002[RHAISTRAT-9017-E002: Conformance documentation update]
    E001 --> E002
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring always last) | The VPAT and accessibility statement must reflect the fixed state of the four flows, so the docs-authoring epic is blocked by the Dashboard implementation epic. Per the docs-authoring priority exception, this edge does not push E002's P2 upstream — E001 remains P1 on its own HLRs. |

No other edges: the two epics touch different components (Dashboard vs
Documentation), different repos, and different work-product types (code vs
content), so there is exactly one implementation epic and one docs epic, with
the single docs-blocking edge.

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic | Notes |
|-----|----------|------|-------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Keyboard operability of the four audited flows. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | **bundled** with HLR-1: focus-indicator consistency is applied to the same controls, modals, and flow surfaces that HLR-1's operability fixes touch — remediating unreachable controls and fixing their focus indicators is one pass over the same audit defect list, so splitting would double-touch every surface. Both HLRs are P1, so no deferral signal exists anyway. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | docs-authoring epic; priority P2 derived from strategy frontmatter `priority: Normal` per the docs-authoring priority exception. |

Full coverage: all three HLRs map to epics; no orphaned requirements.

## Component Mapping

Both strategy components map verbatim to canonical RHAI Jira components
(`Dashboard`, `Documentation` in `.context/rhai-components.txt`) — no
non-obvious mappings. Dashboard is confirmed in-platform by
`.context/architecture-context/architecture/rhoai-3.0/dashboard.md` (owning
team RHOAI Dashboard, public upstream `opendatahub-io/odh-dashboard`), so no
onboarding chain is needed. No architecture context file exists for the
Documentation component (existing docs product, not a new component).

## Health Warnings

- **Epic size overage (E001), deliberately kept:** the four audited flows
  (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run
  submission) with focus traps, unreachable controls, and indicator
  inconsistencies could exceed the ~2-week guideline. It is kept as one epic
  because it is one logical change — a single remediation pass over one audit
  report with one verification walkthrough; splitting per flow would fragment
  the audit traceability and duplicate the keyboard-verification pass.
  **Re-split trigger:** re-split along flow boundaries (one epic per audited
  flow, or operability vs. indicator-consistency if the audit defect list
  shows them separable) if the audit report enumerates materially more defects
  than estimated or remediation of any single flow exceeds ~1 week of effort.
- **Missing strategy sections:** the strategy contains no Impacted Teams
  table, no Dependencies table, no formal Given/When/Then acceptance criteria,
  and no Non-Functional Requirements section. Decomposition proceeded with
  available information; epic ACs were derived from the HLRs and problem
  statement.
- **Documentation team assumed:** with no Impacted Teams table, the
  docs-authoring epic is assigned to a documentation team by convention
  ("RHOAI Documentation"); the owning team should confirm or reassign.
- **VPAT publication process:** the strategy requires an "updated, published
  conformance statement" but does not specify the publication/review channel
  (e.g. whether legal or product sign-off is needed before a VPAT is
  republished). Captured as an acceptance criterion (technical review) per
  HLR-3; if a legal gate exists it belongs to the docs epic's risks, not the
  code epic.

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable — no external dependencies with uncertain timing; the audit
report already enumerates the defects and both deliverables are internal.
